One B-flat guitar riff that a drummer can walk through two ways: six quick steps at 144 or four broad ones at 96 in the same twelve eighths. The tempo map does not change. At 1:00 a different backbeat is all that happens. For the ten seconds either side I checked the written guitars, bass, organ and kick, including lengths and accents: identical after shifting the timestamps. The hat falls from 24 hits to 16, the snare from 12 to 8. This is not a claim that two rendered takes are sample-identical.

At 2:20 the drummer starts switching counts after four phrases, then two, then one. The open notes of the first riff come back as chords before the final D-flat, C, B-flat.

v24, THE LONGER THE STEP, THE BIGGER THE ROOM (whole song; 0:59.6 to 3:20). No note is touched and nothing that was playing is changed: 72 of the song's 167 backbeats are struck a second time into a hall that only its echo comes back from. Not checked by ear; everything below is written or measured.
LISTEN FOR 1:00, the hinge: the riff, the bass and the kick go on exactly as they were, the drummer changes from six quick steps to four broad ones, and the snare, which was a dry crack, now opens a room behind it for about half a second each time. In the swing (2:20-3:00) the room opens and shuts with every change of feet: wet on the broad cells, dry on the quick ones. At 1:20, where he walks two steps a cell, and at 1:29.4, the last stroke before the quiet bridge, the room is longer. At the end (3:07.5 on) the stride lengthens a cell at a time and the room grows with it, and the last backbeat of the song, on the first of the three closing chords at 3:20, is the largest: the door shuts in an empty house.
THE IDEA. The song is one riff under a drummer who walks it two ways, and all that happens at 1:00 is a different backbeat. A slower step leaves a longer wait between backbeats, and that wait was empty: the snare here is a crack of 40 ms (alone against everything else: 7 to 13 dB over it for its first 40 ms in the broad walk, 11 to 16 under by 40-200 ms, 33 to 36 under after). THE LAW: a backbeat that has longer to wait than the quick walk's (more than 8 sixteenths, 0.83 s) rings in a room, and the room is as long as the wait: 12 sixteenths (the broad four: 57 strokes), 16 (the walk in three at 1:50-2:00, and two more: 8 strokes), 24 (the walk in two, 1:20-1:27.5: 3), 36 or more (1:29.4, 3:13.3, 3:16.2 and 3:20: 4). The quick walk's backbeats get nothing, so the door is shut on it. It is the title: one room on one side of the hinge, a bigger one on the other.
WHAT IS WRITTEN. Four tracks, far-12, far-16, far-24, far-36: copies of those snare strokes (same drum, same velocities) each into its own bus, which is a hall with nothing dry in it (decay three times the wait: 3.75, 5, 7.5, 11.25 s; 25 ms before it speaks), cut below 800 Hz and above 6 kHz; faders 0, 0, +1, +3.5 dB.
